name: Act of June 5, 1872 confirming the Osage reservation in Indian Territory
aka: An Act to Confirm to the Great and Little Osage Indians a Reservation in the Indian Territory
promises: Congress confirmed the amended reserve selected for the Osage, bounded east by the 96th meridian, south and west by the Creek country and the Arkansas River, and north by the Kansas line (Royce schedule).
The Osage were to permit the Kansa to settle within it on land not exceeding 160 acres a member, to be paid for by the Kansa (Royce schedule).
today: In Osage Nation v. Irby, 597 F.3d 1117 (10th Cir. 2010), the court held that the reservation established by this Act had been disestablished, affirming summary judgment for Oklahoma tax officials; this went against the Nation.

openQuestions: A reservation confirmation, not a cession. The later allotment of the reservation (Osage Allotment Act of 1906) and the Irby ruling were not researched as breaches of this Act.

The ICC title search for "osage" returned Dockets 9, 105-108 and 126; they concern the 1808, 1818 and 1825 cessions, an 1865 award with offsets, oil royalties paid to Osage County and attorney fees, not the Indian Territory reservation.
